{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 146,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding the read lock",
      "body": "TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock(). In searchSupport.init, the watch goroutine is started immediately before s.search.TotalDocs() is called, and that goroutine can call getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex, which writes to b.cache under cacheMu. Concurrent map iteration and write can trigger a runtime panic (\"concurrent map iteration and map write\"). TotalDocs must take the read lock or operate on a stable snapshot."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 190,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Index startup can permanently miss writes that occur during the build",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, the resource version returned by s.build is discarded (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`), and WatchWriteEvents is started only after all indexes are built. A write that occurs after a namespace has been listed but before WatchWriteEvents captures the latest RV is neither in the initial index nor emitted by the watcher, because the watcher starts from that latest RV. The index can remain stale until another write for that resource occurs or the server restarts. The watcher must be started before/during the build with replay, or the last-read RV from each build must be used to seed the watcher."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Fine-grained cache locking allows duplicate index builds for the same key",
      "body": "getOrCreateIndex checks GetIndex before calling BuildIndex, but with the cacheMu lock now held only at the end of BuildIndex, two concurrent callers for the same key can both see nil, build separate indexes, and both insert into b.cache; the last write wins. The losing caller can still return the discarded index, and file-based builds may concurrently open/create the same directory and fail. This violates the intended single-index-per-key behavior and can cause inconsistent search results or build errors under concurrent access."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 210,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Index event goroutine panics when the watch channel closes",
      "body": "The goroutine reads `v := <-events` forever and passes the result directly to s.handleEvent. WatchWriteEvents implementations, such as the SQL backend's poller, close the channel when they stop. A receive from a closed channel returns a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type/evt.Key, causing a panic during shutdown. The loop should check `v, ok := <-events` and return when the channel is closed. It should also use a cancellable context instead of context.Background() so shutdown can stop it cleanly."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Non-atomic increment in concurrent index initialization",
      "body": "`totalBatchesIndexed++` runs inside group.Go without synchronization while errgroup runs up to s.initWorkers goroutines concurrently. This is a data race, can produce an incorrect count in the trace span, and will be flagged by the race detector. Use an atomic counter or compute the count safely after group.Wait returns."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 451,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Stop flag is no longer checked by RPC methods",
      "body": "The PR removes the `s.Init(ctx)` guard from every RPC entrypoint. Stop sets s.initErr to \"service is stopping\"/\"service is stopped\", but after this change no method reads s.initErr, so requests accepted after Stop can still execute against a stopped backend. A separate readiness/stopping check, or ensuring the gRPC server is fully drained before Stop, is needed to preserve the previous shutdown behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/server/module_server_test.go",
      "line": 36,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Postgres integration test is skipped instead of fixed",
      "body": "The new eager initialization makes this integration test fail on Postgres in CI, and the PR adds a skip with a TODO rather than diagnosing the failure. This removes Postgres coverage for the storage server startup path and may hide a regression in the new initialization ordering. If this is a known environmental issue it should be tracked separately, but skipping the test means the new eager-init path is not verified on Postgres."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding the read lock
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock(). In searchSupport.init, the watch goroutine is started immediately before s.search.TotalDocs() is called, and that goroutine can call getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex, which writes to b.cache under cacheMu. Concurrent map iteration and write can trigger a runtime panic ("concurrent map iteration and map write"). TotalDocs must take the read lock or operate on a stable snapshot.

findings.title: Index startup can permanently miss writes that occur during the build
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, the resource version returned by s.build is discarded (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`), and WatchWriteEvents is started only after all indexes are built. A write that occurs after a namespace has been listed but before WatchWriteEvents captures the latest RV is neither in the initial index nor emitted by the watcher, because the watcher starts from that latest RV. The index can remain stale until another write for that resource occurs or the server restarts. The watcher must be started before/during the build with replay, or the last-read RV from each build must be used to seed the watcher.

findings.title: Fine-grained cache locking allows duplicate index builds for the same key
findings.body: getOrCreateIndex checks GetIndex before calling BuildIndex, but with the cacheMu lock now held only at the end of BuildIndex, two concurrent callers for the same key can both see nil, build separate indexes, and both insert into b.cache; the last write wins. The losing caller can still return the discarded index, and file-based builds may concurrently open/create the same directory and fail. This violates the intended single-index-per-key behavior and can cause inconsistent search results or build errors under concurrent access.

findings.title: Index event goroutine panics when the watch channel closes
findings.body: The goroutine reads `v := <-events` forever and passes the result directly to s.handleEvent. WatchWriteEvents implementations, such as the SQL backend's poller, close the channel when they stop. A receive from a closed channel returns a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type/evt.Key, causing a panic during shutdown. The loop should check `v, ok := <-events` and return when the channel is closed. It should also use a cancellable context instead of context.Background() so shutdown can stop it cleanly.

findings.title: Non-atomic increment in concurrent index initialization
findings.body: `totalBatchesIndexed++` runs inside group.Go without synchronization while errgroup runs up to s.initWorkers goroutines concurrently. This is a data race, can produce an incorrect count in the trace span, and will be flagged by the race detector. Use an atomic counter or compute the count safely after group.Wait returns.

findings.title: Stop flag is no longer checked by RPC methods
findings.body: The PR removes the `s.Init(ctx)` guard from every RPC entrypoint. Stop sets s.initErr to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped", but after this change no method reads s.initErr, so requests accepted after Stop can still execute against a stopped backend. A separate readiness/stopping check, or ensuring the gRPC server is fully drained before Stop, is needed to preserve the previous shutdown behavior.

findings.title: Postgres integration test is skipped instead of fixed
findings.body: The new eager initialization makes this integration test fail on Postgres in CI, and the PR adds a skip with a TODO rather than diagnosing the failure. This removes Postgres coverage for the storage server startup path and may hide a regression in the new initialization ordering. If this is a known environmental issue it should be tracked separately, but skipping the test means the new eager-init path is not verified on Postgres.
